title: Give each existing canonical docs area an index.adoc

values: canonical area directory exists without index.adoc
facts.note: AUTHORITATIVE violation predicate: one of docs/, docs/purpose/, docs/architecture/, docs/architecture/decisions/, docs/archive/ exists in the tree (pre-existing or created by the plan/diff) and has no index.adoc — regardless of file kind or change type. Established by a tree scan (docs_capability validator); a planning-time tree observer is needed to fire before the change lands.

DISCOVERY HINT only: a plan or diff touching the docs tree (including any document at the docs/ root) suggests running the tree predicate. Neither sufficient nor required for firing. docs/dist/** is excluded.
DISCOVERY HINT only: task wording suggests checking the tree; not an alternate trigger and not a gate.

fires: A plan creates docs/architecture/ with documents but no docs/architecture/index.adoc.
A change deletes docs/archive/index.adoc while docs/archive/ still exists.
docs/purpose/ already exists in the tree without index.adoc, even if the current task does not touch it.
docs/ itself has documents but no docs/index.adoc.
doesNotFire: docs/archive/ does not exist in the tree at all.
A non-canonical subdirectory inside an area (e.g. one holding two related documents) has no index.adoc.

given: An authored area (a canonical-tree directory holding authored documents: docs/, docs/purpose/, docs/architecture/, docs/architecture/decisions/, docs/archive/) exists or your plan creates it.
when: It lacks index.adoc, before or after your change.
then: The area MUST contain an index.adoc — its entry point and the node the rendered site navigates to.
prefer: Give the index identity like any document: docs/architecture/index.adoc with `= Architecture`, `:doc-id: architecture.index`, `:status: current`.
Nothing to introduce? Ask whether the area should exist yet, not what its index says; grow the tree only for a real requirement.
docs/architecture/decisions/index.adoc is also a DERIVED registry (planner.docs.adr-registry-derived).
avoid: Ceremonial index/canonical files in every subdirectory or to fill an empty taxonomy; dirs with two related docs need no landing page.
Creating an empty area just to index it.
Do not require an index in docs/dist/.
unless: docs/dist/ is generated output, never required to carry an index.
An absent area is not reported; only an existing area missing its index is.
why: No index means the site can't navigate into the area nor a reader enter it; scoping to canonical areas deliberately avoids ceremonial files.
evidence: docs_capability validator reports no finding: every existing canonical area has an index.adoc.
Reviewer checks each canonical area existing after the change (including docs/ root and untouched pre-existing areas) has index.adoc.
verifier_detail: Check exactly the five canonical areas: docs/, docs/purpose/, docs/architecture/, docs/architecture/decisions/, docs/archive/. Do not require index.adoc in other subdirectories.
Report only when the area directory EXISTS and lacks index.adoc; absent areas are not violations. Directory existence alone is sufficient, independent of file kinds or change type.
audit: Term ids: authored_area (a directory of the canonical tree that holds authored documents; docs/dist/ is not one), index.
References spec 2 §4 (no instantiating filenames to fill an empty taxonomy) and spec 2 §2 Out of scope (images / reference / operations domains not instantiated until justified).

sharedNodes.text: strict: atdd-bun fails on every finding; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: fires/doesNotFire examples, path_glob and task_term discovery hints
additions.justification: Schema requires concrete activation situations; derived from source scope and exceptions, explicitly marked as hints, no new obligation.

additions.text: Creating an empty area just to index it.
additions.justification: Restates source fix_hint (S031–S032) and spec 2 §2 growth principle as an anti-pattern for planners; no new obligation.
